editorial_contributions.text:
Topological properties of axiom-A diffeomorphisms on closed Riemannian manifolds or Markov maps on intervals have been well investigated. In the paper under review, the authors consider the topological and symbolic dynamics for these systems with holes. They fix a Markov partition and then yield a natural representation of the nonwandering set as a subshift of finite type (SFT). The subshift corresponding to the set of points which do not fall in the hole was called an exclusion subshift. Several aspects about the topological structure of exclusion subshifts and their nonwandering sets are investigated.


 They show that every SFT and every \(\beta\)-shift are exclusion shifts, but certain sofic systems are not. They give a criterion for a hole to lead to a SFT and apply this criterion to several different classes of holes with corresponding topologies/measures to show that the ``typical'' hole leads to a SFT. They compare the non-wandering set for the orbits which do not fall in the hole and the nonwandering set of the exclusion shift. They show the finiteness of the number of transitive components in the one-dimensional case, and show that an exclusion subshift has at most countably many topologically transitive components with dense periodic points and exclusion subshifts are always coded systems on such topological transitive components.

editorial_contributions.text: \textit{R. Burton} and \textit{J. E. Steif} [Ergodic Theory Dyn. Sys. 14, No. 2, 213-235 (1994; Zbl 0807.58023)] showed that a higher-dimensional subshift of finite type with the strongest possible topological mixing properties may fail to have a unique measure of maximal entropy, and a maximal measure may fail to be weak-mixing. In this interesting paper, it is shown that many of the properties of maximal measures for topologically mixing subshifts of finite type in one dimension can be recovered for \textsl{nearly} maximal measures, thus giving stronger variational principles for these shifts. The two main results are that for a higher-dimensional subshift of finite type with the \textsl{uniform filling property} the variational principle holds when the supremum is only taken over measures of completely positive entropy, and for such shifts with the additional hypothesis of dense periodic points, the variational principle holds when the supremum is only taken over Bernoulli measures. It is known that the uniform filling property implies that periodic points are dense in dimensions one and two, but in higher dimensions it is not known if this holds.

title.title: Mixing properties of nearly maximal entropy measures for \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) shifts of finite type

editorial_contributions.text:
This interesting paper continues the investigation of the following question. What topological mixing-type conditions on a \(d\)-dimensional subshift of finite type (SFT) ensure that it behaves as a universal model for both topological and measure-theoretic embeddings? An SFT \(Y\) is universal topologically if any SFT \(X\) with \(h_{\text{top}}(X)< h_{\text{top}}(Y)\) and whose points of finite orbit can be embedded into those of \(Y\) is a topological factor of \(Y\). An SFT \(Y\) is universal measurably if, for any ergodic \(d\)-dimensional action \((X,\mu)\) on a nonatomic space, there is a shift-invariant probability measure \(\nu\) on \(Y\) such that \((X,\mu)\) is measurably isomorphic to \((Y,\nu)\). It is well known that both properties hold for \(d=1\) under the weak condition that the SFT be topologically mixing.

 \textit{E. A. Robinson jun.} and \textit{A. A. Şahin} [Monatsh. Math. 132, 237-253 (2001; Zbl 0989.28009)] have shown that a strong topological mixing property called UFP is enough to ensure measurable universality for any \(d\), and \textit{Lightwood} has shown that for \(d=2\) topological mixing and the `square filling' property (together these imply UFP) guarantee topological universality.

 In this paper, a topologically mixing SFT \(Z\) with \(d=2\) is found which has the surprising property that there is a number \(h_0\), \(0<h_0<h_{\text{top}}(Z)\), such that any SFT \(Y\subset Z\) with UFP has \(h_{\text{top}}(Y)\leq h_0\) and any weak-mixing invariant measure \(\mu\) has \(h_{\mu}(Z)\leq h_0\). This is in sharp contrast to the behaviour of SFT with slightly stronger topological mixing properties: if an SFT \(Y\) has UFP and dense periodic points, then \(Y\) satisfies the variational principle with respect to measures of completely positive entropy.
